7qyh1o:203: Traditional diffusion model improvements usually happen at the training stage (collecting more data, adjusting loss functions). HITS extends the improvement process to test-time, progressively raising quality through multiple rounds of refine. This idea is consistent with recent works on test-time compute scaling. However, HITS's hierarchical design (boundary frames first, then full clips) is an engineering compromise — iterative refinement on full videos is extremely expensive, so processing boundary frames first concentrates the compute budget on the most critical positions.
8zie43:243: A²RD's core insight is decoupling "creative composition" from "consistency enforcement". Traditional end-to-end models attempt to perform content generation and consistency maintenance simultaneously in a single forward pass, which creates inconsistent training objectives—the model must balance between "generating interesting content" and "staying consistent with what came before", and often neither is optimal. A²RD decomposes this contradiction into two relatively independent sub-problems by introducing an Agent-based workflow and Memory mechanism: the generator is responsible for "creation", while the Agent + Memory handle "recall and planning". This decoupling is easier to implement in engineering because the generator and the consistency module can be optimized separately.
